red_interpretation: In this particular blueprint the construction marks are drawn in fine gray/black line work (pixel scan found zero red pixels), but they carry the standard red-line meaning of the back category: (1) the band of short, irregular vertical strokes directly below the yoke seam is hand-gathered shirring — the Neapolitan "grinze" where the back body is gathered into the yoke; (2) the two long vertical lines in the body are stitched dart seams for waist suppression. The sibling "Double Darts" blueprint draws the identical two dart lines in red, confirming they are dart seams, not stripes or contrast fabric. Nothing here is contrast fabric; everything renders as real gathers and stitched seams in white cloth.
geometry_summary: Rear view, 209x243 px tech pack. One straight horizontal yoke seam spans the full back width at y=47 (~24% of drawing height); body side seams at x≈45 and x≈162 (body width ≈117 px, center-back x≈104). Directly below the yoke seam, a shirring band of many fine, irregular, vertical gather strokes extends y=48–71 (≈24 px, ~13% of the 185 px yoke-to-hem length), densest at the seam and tapering out — Neapolitan hand-gathered fullness across nearly the whole width between armholes; there are NO pleat folds. Two symmetric vertical darts, each drawn as a single seam line: left at x=72, right at x=137, i.e. each ≈23% of body width in from its side seam (≈54% of the half-width out from center-back, ≈56% of body width apart). Both darts run y=103–201: starting ≈30% below the yoke seam (shoulder-blade level) and ending ≈83% down (high hip), length ≈53% of yoke-to-hem, terminating ≈31 px above the lowest hem point. Curved shirttail hem, lowest at center (y≈232), rising toward the sides (y≈225). No center-back seam, no pleats, no other interior lines. Long sleeves hang at the sides with sleeve plackets and buttoned barrel cuffs; back collar band and collar visible above the yoke.
counts: Pleats: 0 (no box, inverted, or side pleats). Darts: 2 (one per side, each drawn as a single vertical seam line — not paired stitch rows). Yoke seams: 1 (straight, horizontal, full width). Gather/shirring bands: 1 (continuous, directly below the yoke seam, nearly armhole to armhole). Other seams visible in rear view: 2 side seams, 2 armhole seams, 1 curved hem; no center-back seam.
locked_features: Single straight horizontal yoke seam across the full back width, sitting at normal upper-back height

Neapolitan hand-gathered shirring (grinze) directly below the yoke seam: a dense band of many fine, slightly irregular vertical gathers spanning nearly the full width between the armholes, releasing soft vertical fullness ripples that fade out within the upper back
Exactly two vertical waist darts, symmetric about center-back, each a single crisp stitched seam
Dart placement at the back quarter-points: each dart ~23% of the back width in from its side seam (well outboard of center-back)
Darts are long: starting at shoulder-blade level (~30% below the yoke seam) and ending at high hip (~83% down), i.e. ~half the yoke-to-hem length, ending clearly above the hem curve
Zero pleats anywhere — the gathered yoke provides all upper-back fullness
No center-back seam; the panel between the darts is clean
Curved shirttail hem, longest at center-back, rising toward the side seams
Long sleeves with sleeve plackets and buttoned barrel cuffs hanging naturally at the sides
Back collar band and turned-down collar visible above the yoke
ratios: Yoke seam height: ~24% down the total rear-view drawing; yoke-to-hem length is the reference unit (185 px)
Shirring band depth: ~13% of yoke-to-hem length (roughly 3–4 cm on a real shirt), densest at the seam and tapering
Dart start: ~30% of yoke-to-hem below the yoke seam; dart end: ~83% down; dart length ~53% of yoke-to-hem (a long dart, roughly 25–28 cm real-world)
Dart lateral position: each dart ~23% of body width in from its side seam / ~54% of the half-width out from center-back; darts ~56% of body width apart
Dart lower end terminates ~17% of yoke-to-hem length above the lowest hem point
Hem curve drop: center-back hem sits ~7 px (~4% of yoke-to-hem) below the side-seam hem
uncertain: Number of stitch rows per dart and pressing direction — each dart is drawn as one single line, so I lock one visible seam per dart, but whether the fold is pressed toward or away from center-back is not determinable
Exact count and depth of the shirring gathers — drawn as ~20–30 irregular hand strokes of varying length; density is approximate, band depth ~3–4 cm is an estimate from the 13% ratio
Whether the darts taper closed at both ends (fish dart) — the drawing shows uniform straight lines with no width/taper indication
